name: Aquatint
summary: A way to bite a tone into a copper plate with acid through a ground of rosin dust. The print has a grain like a wash.
how: Dust the plate with rosin and heat it, so that each grain sticks; use a grain of about 100 to 150 to the inch.
Bite the plate in acid in timed baths; each longer bath gives a darker step.
Stop out the light areas with varnish before each bath; this gives hard edges between the steps.
Print with the plate wiped in one warm black or sepia; a plate mark of 3 mm to 6 mm shows round the image.

origin.note: Jean-Baptiste Le Prince made aquatints in 1768 to 1769; other makers also claim the invention.

adoptions.via: Francisco Goya publishes Los Caprichos with etched line and deep aquatint tones.
